name: Sindhi
variety: Standard Sindhi based on the Vicholi (central, 'Middle') dialect of Sindh, written in the Perso-Arabic Sindhi script
sources: Nihalani, Paroo (1995). Sindhi. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 25(2), 95-98; reprinted in Handbook of the International Phonetic Association (1999), Cambridge University Press, 131-134.
Nihalani, Paroo (1974). An aerodynamic study of stops in Sindhi. Phonetica 29, 193-224.
Nihalani, Paroo (1986). Phonetic implementation of implosives. Language and Speech 29(3), 253-262.
Khubchandani, Lachman M. (2003). Sindhi. In Cardona, George & Jain, Dhanesh (eds.), The Indo-Aryan Languages. London: Routledge.
Keerio, Ayaz (2010). Acoustic Analysis of Sindhi Speech: A Pre-curser for an ASR System. DPhil thesis, University of Sussex.
Ladefoged, Peter & Maddieson, Ian (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Oxford: Blackwell.
Trumpp, Ernest (1872). Grammar of the Sindhi Language. London: Trübner.
Masica, Colin P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
Khan, Sameer ud Dowla (2016). The intonation of South Asian languages: towards a comparative analysis. Proceedings of Formal Approaches to South Asian Languages 6, 23-36.

vowel_formants.speaker: adult male (mean of 15 speakers of the Middle, i.e. Vicholi, dialect)
vowel_formants.notes: The other four dialects in the same table (Utradi, Thareli, Lari, Lasi) differ by up to about 50 Hz in F1 and 100 Hz in F2.

contrasts: five-way contrast in voiced and voiceless stops at the labial, retroflex, palatal and velar places: voiceless unaspirated, voiceless aspirated, voiced, breathy voiced and voiced implosive (/p pʰ b bʱ ɓ/); the dental place has no implosive
four voiced implosives /ɓ ɗ ʄ ɠ/; the coronal one is retroflex or postalveolar [ᶑ]
plain versus breathy voiced (aspirated) sonorants: /m n ɳ l ɽ/ : /mʱ nʱ ɳʱ lʱ ɽʱ/
four nasal places /m n ɳ ɲ ŋ/, with /ɲ/ and /ŋ/ as independent phonemes
ten vowels: short /ɪ ə ʊ/ against long peripheral /i e ɛ ɑ ɔ o u/
consonant gemination is marginal: old geminate voiced stops became the implosives
allophony: implosives are made with a lowered larynx; voicing is strong and its amplitude grows during the closure, whereas it decays during the closure of the plain and breathy voiced stops (Nihalani 1986; Keerio 2010)
the palatal implosive /ʄ/ does not show the growth of voicing amplitude that the other three show (Keerio 2010)

mean closure durations of implosives between vowels are 97 ms for /ɓ/, 94 ms for the retroflex, 74 ms for /ʄ/ and 82 ms for /ɠ/, with F0 of 156-167 Hz during the closure for male speakers (Keerio 2010, Table 8.2)
the palatal stops are affricated ([tɕ dʑ])
vowels are nasalised next to nasal consonants
word-final short vowels are very short and may be dropped in fast speech
syllable_structure: (C)(C)V(C); native words end in a vowel; clusters are few and occur mainly in loans
phonotactics: every native word ends in a vowel; final short /ə ɪ ʊ/ carry gender, number and case and are normally not written
/ɳ ɽ ŋ ɲ/ do not occur word-initially
implosives occur initially and medially and are never aspirated
loan consonants /f z x ɣ/ (and /q/ in careful speech) come from Persian and Arabic

stress.rule: Prominence is usually on the first syllable of the stem, with long vowels attracting it; no instrumental study that I can cite.
stress.cues: not established; pitch of the phrasal rise and duration

rhythm.vowel_reduction: final short vowels are shortened and may be lost; no quality reduction of long vowels
rhythm.notes: Class and final lengthening are assumptions from the areal pattern; no measurement could be verified.

length.notes: Mean vowel durations for male speakers of the Middle dialect: long /i/ 126, /e/ 135, /ɛ/ 141, /ɑ/ 152, /ɔ/ 135, /o/ 125, /u/ 135 ms; short /ɪ/ 81, /ə/ 83, /ʊ/ 72 ms, so a long vowel is about 1.6 to 1.8 times a short one (Keerio 2010).

intonation.declarative: a chain of rising phrases, one per content word with its clitics, low at the start and high at the end; the final phrase falls to a low boundary
intonation.yes_no_question: rising phrases and a high final boundary
intonation.wh_question: as a declarative, low final boundary
intonation.continuation: high right edge on non-final phrases
intonation.notes: Rising phrases are reported by Khan 2016 for the recording of Nihalani's illustration; the sentence-type boundary tones are the typical South Asian pattern given there, not a separate Sindhi study.

phonation: voiced implosives with lowered larynx and strong, growing voicing during closure
breathy voiced stops /bʱ d̪ʱ ɖʱ dʑʱ ɡʱ/
breathy voiced sonorants /mʱ nʱ ɳʱ lʱ ɽʱ/

problems: The four implosives are mapped to the plain voiced stops: ٻ gives [b], ڏ gives [ɖ], ڄ gives [ɟ], ڳ gives [ɡ], the same output as ب, ڊ, ج, گ. The implosive contrast, the most characteristic feature of Sindhi, is lost completely; the phoneme table has no implosive phonemes.
ٿ (dental aspirated) becomes the retroflex unaspirated stop when the inherent vowel follows (ٿر [ʈʌr], هٿ [hʌʈ]); the rule has t. where t# is meant.
ڱ (velar nasal) is mapped to the syllabic nasal phoneme N-, a vowel-type segment.
Breathy sonorants are a sonorant plus separate [h] with inserted vowels (ماڻهو [maːɳhuː], ڳالهه [ɡaːləhʌh]).
The word-final short vowels are never produced (ٻار [baːr], هٿ [hʌʈ]); unwritten short vowels inside words are guessed as schwa and then subjected to the Hindi schwa-deletion logic.
The rules are an adaptation of the Urdu rules and still contain Urdu word entries; /r/ is the trill [R].
Breathy voiced stops come from the Hindi base table (voiced closure plus voiceless aspiration sample); /ɦ/ is voiceless [h].
Sindhi written in Devanagari is handed to the Nepali voice.
Intonation uses the generic eSpeak tunes.
good: aspirated and unaspirated letters are kept apart (ک [kʰ] : ڪ [k], ڦ [pʰ], ٺ [ʈʰ])
retroflex nasal, palatal nasal and retroflex flap are present
long and short vowel pairs differ in quality and length

notes: The consonant chart follows Nihalani's illustration; he writes the palatal series with c, ɟ. The implosives go back to Old and Middle Indo-Aryan geminate and word-initial voiced stops. No VOT table could be verified: Keerio 2010 reports release durations for stops in medial position, but with a different definition from VOT, so voice_onset_time_ms is left out.
